This development constructs their categories, Hecke algebras, induction, Jacquet functors and adjunctions, then studies admissibility and spherical representations through Satake theory. Integral coefficient families and finiteness results extend the framework beyond complex representations, supporting local Langlands theory and its arithmetic applications.

name: SpecialValuesBirchTate
title: Birch–Tate and arithmetic special-value formulas
summary: The Birch–Tate formula relates a special value of a totally real number field's zeta function to the size of its second algebraic K-group. This development follows the odd-primary and two-primary arguments, including abelian-field cases, and accounts for the Euler factors introduced by S-integers. Independent calculations over the rationals provide examples, while higher special-value statements connect the theorem to broader arithmetic conjectures.

name: StableHomotopyKTheory
title: Homotopy foundations for algebraic K-theory
summary: Higher algebraic K-theory relies on homotopy constructions that turn categories and groups into spaces and spectra. This development builds nerves, classifying spaces, homotopy fibres, Quillen's theorems and the plus construction. Group completion and spectrum foundations connect these models to stable invariants. Coefficients, completion and spectral sequences then provide the tools for comparing K-theoretic constructions and calculating their arithmetic consequences.

name: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure
title: Reusable infrastructure for torsion in arithmetic cohomology
summary: Torsion classes in the cohomology of arithmetic spaces carry information invisible to characteristic-zero cohomology. This development connects integral sheaves and formal models with perfectoid period maps, automorphic bundles and approximating sections. It compares coherent, completed and torsion cohomology while tracking Hecke actions. Boundary induction and determinant factorizations provide the structures needed to transport this information into arithmetic representation theory.

name: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic
title: Berkovich spaces, tropical curves and nonarchimedean arithmetic
summary: Berkovich and tropical geometry turn parts of nonarchimedean geometry into spaces with visible metric and combinatorial structure. This development constructs analytic spectra, discs, annuli and the skeletons of semistable curves. Divisors, slope formulas and tropical multiplicities connect those models to algebraic geometry. Faithful tropicalization, model metrics and measures then support local heights, uniformization and integration in arithmetic geometry.

name: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories
title: Roadmap: Artin v-stacks, solid and lisse coefficient categories
summary: Sheaves on Artin v-stacks provide a setting for the geometric form of the local Langlands program. This development builds the relevant operations, local acyclicity and smoothness criteria, then introduces condensed, solid and lisse coefficient categories. Sheaves on strata of the moduli stack of bundles connect the geometry to smooth representations. Compact generation, duality and admissibility organize the resulting categories.

name: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals
title: Roadmap: isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces
summary: Vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve translate p-adic linear algebra into geometry. This development relates isocrystals and slopes to bundles, cohomology, ampleness and geometric classification, while retaining the additional structure needed for varying bases. Banach–Colmez spaces describe the associated linear geometry. Relative Harder–Narasimhan strata then organize how bundles and their slope decompositions vary in families.

name: WeightsInEtaleCohomology
title: Roadmap: Weights and purity in étale cohomology
summary: Weights measure the sizes of Frobenius eigenvalues in the étale cohomology of varieties over finite fields. This development brings together the weight and purity results needed for arithmetic applications, beginning with curves and abelian varieties. Nearby cycles, Lefschetz pencils and monodromy supply the geometric reductions. The resulting comparisons support automorphic Galois representations, compatible systems and cohomological interpretations of zeta functions.

name: WeilConjectures
title: Weil conjectures and cohomological zeta functions
summary: The zeta function of a variety over a finite field records its points over every finite extension. This development connects that generating function to Frobenius acting on cohomology and assembles rationality, the functional equation and the Riemann-hypothesis bounds in their appropriate geometric settings. Duality, weights and comparison theorems also yield point-counting estimates, with curves supplying concrete geometric examples.
